sources.update: git -C ~/.agents/references/TokenEconomizer fetch && git -C ~/.agents/references/TokenEconomizer checkout <SHA> && claude plugin update tokeneconomizer@tokeneconomizer
sources.decision: 2026-11-16 owner named it: installed as a trial. Apache-2.0, stdlib Python, no telemetry; hooks on SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse(+Failure), Stop and SessionEnd, none on PreToolUse, never blocks. Defaults were unsafe here (toolprune=auto writes permissions.deny, its own model calls use Haiku), so global config is enabled=false, toolprune=propose with a protect list (Workflow, SendMessage, ListAgents, ScheduleWakeup, Cron*, worktrees, Monitor, PushNotification, SendUserFile, the browser MCPs, railway, exa), microskills=envfacts (no model calls), loopguard=nudge with claude_paid_model=sonnet at low effort. Enabled in nebi-skill, cnlsneakers and ecommerce-workspace (the three busiest repos over 30 days) after a history import of 33, 94 and 46 sessions. Nebi's hooks skip its `claude -p` sidecalls (TE_SIDECALL=1).
sources.why: Learns from past sessions per repo: proposes dropping tools a repo never uses, states repeated facts at session start, nudges a stuck turn once.
sources.notes: The plugin runs from the clone (marketplace 'tokeneconomizer', user scope; settings.json and plugins are shared by all three config dirs). CLI: ~/.agents/references/TokenEconomizer/plugin/scripts/te (or ~/.tokeneconomizer/bin/te once a hook has run). After a week: `te status` in each trial repo (effective tokens per session, plugin overhead, proposed tools). Its first proposal in nebi-skill lists several hundred never-used claude.ai connector tools; apply only ever with named tools (`te toolprune apply <tool> ...`), never bare: the stored proposals (545 tools in nebi-skill, 728 in ecommerce-workspace, 1,432 in cnlsneakers) include tools in real use. The global protect list (repo-level lists replace it, so keep it global) covers the browser MCPs, railway, exa, the claude.ai connectors in use (Shopify, Supabase, Higgsfield, ElevenLabs, Canva, Gmail, Google Drive, Claude Docs, Mobbin), namecheap, domain-check, Roblox Studio, plugin MCPs and core deferred tools. settings.json env carries TE_TOOLPRUNE=propose and TE_CLAUDE_PAID_MODEL=sonnet so a lost config.json cannot fall back to auto-prune and Haiku. Do not run `te toolprune measure` or `refresh-catalog`: both hardcode Haiku. Rollback: disable the plugin, `te toolprune restore` in each repo, remove ~/.tokeneconomizer. Cost: a Python start per tool call (about 0.1 s) in every session, even where it is disabled. ~/.tokeneconomizer is shared by every account.
